Subject: Post-demo recap & asks — Veridian infra, auth, embeddings, dedicated sizing

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick written recap + 1) confirmations we need from your side and 2) clear asks for engineering so we can produce a sizing/pricing package.

Key takeaways from today's demo:
- Primary workloads: document summarization + semantic search + a reranker stage for top-K refinement. Tool-calling required for PDF extraction and a structured JSON response (function-like output).
- Security: customer SSO + SCIM for user provisioning; preference for OIDC-based auth for service-to-service tokens.
- Target latency: sub-500ms p90 for short prompts; embeddings/reranker can tolerate higher tail latencies (p95 ~ 1.5s).
- Expected traffic: peak ~150 req/s, typical steady ~40–60 req/s; avg prompt length ~120 tokens in, expected generated tokens ~180.

Clarifications we need from you (please reply inline):
1) Will all requests be multitenant behind a single API key per tenant, or do you want VPC-private/Private deployment per environment?
2) Confirm burst behaviour — are there short spikes up to 300 rps for batch jobs?
3) Embeddings: will they be batched from a separate ingestion pipeline (recommended) or inline with user requests?
4) Reranker: is it a lightweight dot-product reranker or a small cross-encoder you expect Redwood to host for you?

Engineering asks (owners copied):
- SDK & auth: prefer to be explicit — language first: JS + Py support required; we need to know if you expect OAuth/OIDC flows for end-users or only service tokens for server-to-server. (owner: Karthik)
- Routing & tool-calling: structured output JSON schema for the tool calls and a short example invocation for the PDF extractor (owner: Rishi)
- Dedicated sizing: initial ask is conservative — please confirm desired baseline GPU count / region and whether you want reserved capacity + autoscale. (owner: Laura)

Attachments: veridian-infra-requirements.xlsx (your draft), arch-sketch.png (sketch from call). I've also attached a draft SLA we can iterate on.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: reply with the four clarifications above by EOD Friday so engineering can size.
- Rishi/Karthik/Laura: review and propose an initial dedicated sizing + auth/SDK plan by Wed next week.

Thanks — Soojin

Thanks Soojin — great summary. Answers inline below.

1) Multitenancy model: single Veridian account with tenant-scoped API keys. We will not run separate VPCs for each tenant initially. We are evaluating a Private/VPC deployment for sensitive accounts later in H2.
2) Burst behaviour: yes — we run nightly ingestion that can spike for short windows up to ~280–320 rps for 3–5 minutes. External traffic spikes expected ~2–3x baseline for short events.
3) Embeddings: separate ingestion pipeline will batch embeddings; we expect batch sizes of 512–1024 on the ingestion path. Inference-time embeddings (user search) will happen inline but at lower qps (~20–30 rps).
4) Reranker: we plan to start with a lightweight cross-encoder (smaller cross-encoder model) that re-scores the top 50 candidates from an ANN index.

Additional notes:
- Auth: we prefer OIDC for admin SSO + short-lived service tokens for server-to-server (rotation via KMS).
- SDKs: JS + Python required; our frontend uses JS and backend batchers in Python.
- Structured output: we'll share a minimal JSON schema for the extractor tool (fields: title, authors[], page_count, sections[]).
- Capacity ask: initial commitment target is 2x A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west. We'll consider expanding to eu-west later.

I've attached an updated spreadsheet with some traffic profiles (veridian-infra-requirements.xlsx). Happy to hop on a quick 30m follow-up after engineering proposes sizing.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-demo recap & asks — Veridian infra, auth, embeddings, dedicated sizing

Thanks — quick technical read and recommendations below (high level; we can turn into a one-page sizing and cost estimate):

Assumptions from Alex: peak 320 rps spikes (3–5m), steady 40–60 rps, avg request tokens = 120 in + 180 out = ~300 tokens/request. Embeddings ingestion batched 512–1024; embeddings queries ~20–30 rps. Reranker is a small cross-encoder scoring top-50.

1) Model choice & pools
- Recommend separating pools: gen pool (for text gen + tool-calls), embeddings pool, and reranker pool. This lets us tune quantization / kernel selection independently and avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Gen model: use a quantized 4-bit optimized variant (latency-optimized kernel). Expect ~60–90k tokens/s per A100-equivalent for short contexts if batched effectively. With 300 tokens/request at 150 req/s baseline => 45k tok/s; peak 320 rps => ~96k tok/s. So baseline of 1 A100-equivalent may be tight under sustained peak; recommend baseline 2 GPUs with autoscale to 4 for sustained peaks.

2) Autoscale & queueing
- Autoscale policy (suggested): baseline 2 GPUs; scale +1 node when queue length > 40 for 60s; scale up more aggressively (burst policy) when instantaneous rps > 1.8x baseline for 30s. Max scale to 4 nodes. Scale down after 10m idle.
- Queue strategy: per-tenant ingress queue + global dispatch queue. Per-tenant soft quota prevents one tenant from starving others during ingestion spikes. Global queue depth target = 200 requests; per-tenant cap = 50 by default (configurable).

3) Concurrency & batching
- Concurrency per GPU: target ~48–64 inflight requests depending on token length; enforce max concurrency per worker to limit KV cache pressure. Use dynamic batching window up to 30ms to form larger batches on steady traffic.
- For embeddings ingestion: dedicate an embedding worker pool (FP16) with high batch sizes and lower concurrency; batch sizes 512–1024 for throughput jobs.

4) Reranker
- Host reranker in CPU+smaller GPU pool depending on model; small cross-encoder can be served on a single mid-sized GPU if quantized; plan for 2 nodes to allow redundancy and rolling upgrades.
- Alternatively, consider running reranker as a scaled service in the customer's infra if low-latency re-ranking is critical — but preferred to host for consistent ops.

5) Auth & SDK
- OIDC + short-lived service tokens (rotated via KMS) is supported; we will provide SDK hooks for token refresh + example code for SSO flows.

6) Observability & fallbacks
- Strongly recommend prefix KV caching for common prompts and deterministic tool-call results. Enable fallback routing to a cheaper model variant if queueing latency exceeds SLO.

Open questions for Alex (to confirm sizing):
- Confirm tokens/request distribution (p10/p50/p90) and proportion of requests that trigger tool-calls (tool-calls increase response tokens and latency).
- Any GDPR/PII retention constraints that affect cache lifetimes or private deployment needs?

I'll draft a one-page sizing with cost multiplier estimates based on 2->4 GPU baseline and send by EOD tomorrow.

Adding operational knobs and a recommended rollout plan:

Autoscale policy (refined):
- Baseline: 2 GPUs (us-west). Burst pool: 1–2 additional warm nodes (keep warm for 5–10 minutes).
- Scale-up triggers: queue length > 40 sustained for 60s OR observed rps > 1.9x baseline for 30s.
- Scale-down: sustained queue < 10 and rps < 0.8x baseline for 10m.

Queueing & backpressure:
- Accept requests at edge, return 202 + request-id when request is queued > 2s with an estimated wait-time header. Customers can poll or use webhooks.
- Per-tenant fairness: token-bucket rate limiting per tenant + global emergency reserve.

Concurrency limits and timeouts:
- Per-worker max concurrency = 64 for gen pool (reduce to 32 for long-context jobs). Request timeout = 30s by default; allow customer override for batch jobs.

Tool-calling / structured output:
- We will support function/tool calling with strict schema validation at the gateway. Recommend Veridian provide canonical JSON schema and a small set of example tool responses for the extractor.
- Route tool-calls to a separate worker type that has sandboxed runtime for safe execution.

Rollout plan for Dedicated capacity:
1) PoC phase (2 weeks): spin up 2 GPUs in us-west, configure SDK keys and OIDC test flow, run synthetic traffic matching their p50/p90 distribution.
2) Load validation (1 week): run ingestion batches + synthetic spikes to validate autoscale triggers and queueing behaviour.
3) Canary (2 weeks): route 10% production traffic, enable fallbacks to cheaper model variant at 5% error rate.
4) Production: finalize SLA, commit to baseline with 24/7 support add-on.

Action items:
- Rishi: send the one-pager sizing + estimated token throughput numbers (EOD tomorrow).
- Soojin: request token distribution (p10/p50/p90), percent of requests that call tools, and any retention/GDPR constraints from Alex.
- Laura: prepare a draft pricing appendix for the dedicated pool (2->4 GPUs, burst add-on).

I'll join the next sync with Alex if helpful.

— Karthik
